questions.s: General plan of the autonomic system (Last's):
o: Grey rami carry postganglionic efferent fibres
Last's.
White rami carry preganglionic and visceral afferent fibres
Last's.
The suprarenal glands receive both sympathetic and parasympathetic supply
Suprarenals and gonads have only sympathetic supply.
Parasympathetic fibres supply the limbs
Parasympathetic supply is wholly visceral.

questions.s: Last's notes that lumbar sympathectomy at L1:
o: May compromise ejaculation
Last's.
Abolishes bladder emptying
Detrusor is parasympathetic.
Abolishes penile erection
Erection is parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnic).
Removes vasoconstrictor supply to parts of the lower limb
Grey rami to lumbar nerves carry vasoconstrictor fibres to the lower limb.
Each has parasympathetic, sympathetic and sensory roots
Last's.
Only the parasympathetic fibres synapse in them
Last's.
The dorsal vagal nucleus relays in a named cranial ganglion
Its fibres relay in the walls of the viscera.
The sympathetic roots come from T5 to T8
From T1-3 via the superior cervical ganglion.

questions.s: Sympathetic roots of the cranial ganglia (Last's):
o: The ciliary ganglion receives sympathetics from the ICA plexus
Last's.
The otic ganglion receives sympathetics with the middle meningeal artery
Last's.
The submandibular ganglion receives sympathetics from the ICA plexus
From the facial artery plexus (ECA).
The pterygopalatine ganglion receives sympathetics with the maxillary artery
Via the deep petrosal nerve from the ICA plexus.
Its parasympathetic root is the lesser petrosal nerve
From the inferior salivary nucleus.
It has a somatic motor root from the nerve to medial pterygoid
Unique among the cranial ganglia.
Its secretomotor fibres reach the parotid via the facial nerve
Via the auriculotemporal nerve.
Motor fibres to tensor tympani synapse in it
They pass through without synapse.
The ciliary parasympathetic root comes via the nerve to inferior oblique
Last's.
The ciliary sensory root comes from the nasociliary nerve
Last's.
The pterygopalatine sensory root comes from the mandibular nerve
From the maxillary nerve.
Pterygopalatine postganglionic lacrimal fibres travel in the nasociliary nerve
Via the zygomatic and lacrimal nerves.
Cranial visceral afferent cell bodies lie in the inferior ganglia of IX and X
Last's.
Pelvic visceral afferent cell bodies lie in the S2-4 posterior root ganglia
Last's.
Cranial visceral afferents end in the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus
In the nucleus of the tractus solitarius.
About 10% of abdominal vagal fibres are afferent
About 90%.
It enters behind the medial arcuate ligament
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
The right trunk lies behind the IVC
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
The common iliac vessels lie behind the trunks at the pelvic brim
They lie in front. (Last's p. 365)
There are usually six lumbar ganglia
Usually four. (Last's p. 365)

questions.s: Branches of the lumbar sympathetic trunk (Last's):
o: Grey rami pass to all five lumbar nerves
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
The superior hypogastric plexus lies in front of L5
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
White rami reach all five lumbar nerves
Only the first two lumbar nerves give white rami. (Last's p. 365)
The "presacral nerve" lies in front of the sacrum
It is a misnomer: it is prelumbar. (Last's p. 365)
The lesser splanchnic nerve comes from T10 and T11
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
The least splanchnic relays in a renal ganglion
Last's. (Last's p. 365)
The greater splanchnic nerve comes from T1 to T4
From T5 to T9. (Last's p. 365)
Coeliac fibres to the suprarenal medulla are the secretomotor supply
Preganglionic splanchnic fibres reach the medulla without relay; postganglionic coeliac fibres are vasomotor. (Last's p. 365)
The parasympathetic is the main motor supply to the bladder
Last's. (Last's p. 380)
Sympathetic fibres contract the superficial trigone
And the male internal sphincter. (Last's p. 380)
Bladder distension sensation travels with sympathetic fibres
With parasympathetic fibres. (Last's p. 380)
Rectal pain travels only with sympathetic fibres
With both. (Last's p. 380)
